intro_html: Honey sesame chicken is sweet, sticky, and just plain fun to eat, and it comes in as an easy, budget-friendly bowl. It is high protein, low fat, and tastes like the good takeout without the sticker shock. One batch makes 14 servings.
cost_closing_html: About $3.45 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings runs about 57g protein for roughly 562 calories, at around $1.95 a bowl.
upsell_html: Sticky, sweet, and easy on the wallet, this one makes prepping ahead feel like a reward. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Plain ketchup and honey team up for that sweet-savory glaze without any bottled specialty sauce.
A little sesame oil goes a long way, so one bottle flavors many batches.
Buy the chicken breast in a value pack to keep every bowl affordable.
make_it: Add the chicken breast and minced garlic to the crock.
Pour in the soy sauce, ketchup, honey, and a splash of sesame oil.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours until the chicken is tender.
Shred the chicken, then whisk the cornstarch with a little water and stir it in to thicken the glaze.
Steam the broccoli and cook the rice.
Serve the honey sesame chicken over rice with broccoli.
